subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats automatically provision persistent sender-specific agents, and what authorization, quota, lifecycle, and shared/private memory contract should gate that behavior?
rationale: The request is not a narrow bug fix; it creates durable agents, workspaces, configs, skills, memory namespaces, and message-routing authority from group-chat identities.

options.title: Design Generic Contract First
options.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel-owned surface.

options.title: Keep Session-Only Routing
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope and explicit subagent/thread mechanisms, documenting full per-user agent orchestration as a separate deployment or plugin pattern for now.

options.title: Reject Automatic Provisioning
options.body: Close the feature direction if maintainers decide group identities should never create durable OpenClaw agents automatically.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Contract First
recommendation.body: Create a generic admin-authorized identity-to-agent lifecycle and memory contract, then let Feishu implement it as one channel-owned surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses Feishu routing and core subagent/thread-binding architecture, where steipete has the freshest source ownership signal.
